transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-25 09:00-09:48 UTC | Duration 48m
Attendees: Alice (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Kelsey (Redwood CSM) — Jenna (Westbridge Head of ML), Marco (Infra), Priya (Security), Samir (Product)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on security, networking, pilot scope and timeline. Primary asks: SOC2 artifacts, VPC/on-prem checklist, pilot traffic pattern + success criteria, and scheduling a technical deep dive.

Topics: onboarding runbook; VPC vs hosted; data residency; KMS/HSM options; rollout/rollback; pilot timeline and metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alice from Redwood inference, I'm the AE on the account, with Devon our SE and Kelsey from CS. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jenna - Westbridge: Morning, doing well thanks, excited to get this going, we've been looking at the doc you sent, a few questions on the private deployment path.
[00:15] Devon (Redwood SE): Great, yeah today we wanted to cover three things — security/artifacts, networking options (VPC / private install), and the pilot scope. then we can lock dates.
[00:25] Marco - Westbridge: Quick note, infra-wise we run primarily in GCP, but we have an air-gapped environment for PII workloads, so we're interested in both VPC peering and the on-prem package you mentioned in the doc — is that a hard lift?
[00:36] Devon (Redwood SE): Not necessarily, we support a couple of on-prem flows, the package requires an initial private control plane handshake — apologies if the term in the doc is off, sometimes the transcript spells it odd — but basically a secure tunnel and customer-managed KMS. we can walk through the checklist.
[00:49] Priya - Westbridge: On KMS — we need HSM-backed keys and audit logs, we are SOC2 and PCI adjacent so the HSM requirement is pretty firm. also SSO SAML integration is a must.
[01:02] Alice (Redwood): Totally, we have HSM integrations and SAML SSO — i'll send the SOC2 and a short summary of the HSM options after the call.
[01:10] Samir - Westbridge: And we want to understand the latency tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated vs private. our product team wants P95 under 200ms for short completions, but we also have batch reranks that can tolerate more.
[01:24] Devon (Redwood SE): That's a good callout — dedicated reserved capacity is easiest to guarantee latency at scale, hosted can be fast but depends on multi-tenant variability; private on-prem will be as fast as your infra and network path. for the pilot we usually recommend dedicated or a private staging lane to see realistic numbers.
[01:40] Jenna - Westbridge: Are there any quick knobs we should try to keep costs down? quantization or caching?
[01:45] Devon (Redwood SE): Yes — batching policies, KV-cache prefix caching and model quantization profiles are the main levers. we can propose config tuned for your mix; i'll include recommendations in the runbook.
[01:56] Priya - Westbridge: About telemetry — we need retention of audit logs for 12 months and token-level visibility for compliance. is that supported out of the box?
[02:06] Kelsey (Redwood CSM): We can enable longer retention as an add-on, and the Console provides token-level breakdowns. we'll outline retention pricing in the packet.
[02:16] Jenna - Westbridge: Perfect. also one more thing on data residency — some EU customers require data stay in EU region — can we pin regionals per-route?
[02:25] Devon (Redwood SE): Yes, smart routing supports region pinning per route and fallback policies. we'll show how that looks in the demo next week.
[02:34] Marco - Westbridge: For networking, do you support both VPC peering and private link style connectors? we prefer peering but also want minimal network ops.
[02:43] Devon (Redwood SE): We support peering and private-link-like options; the initial setup differs — peering needs route tables and firewall rules, private-link needs endpoint services. i'll send a checklist with pictures.
[02:56] Samir - Westbridge: On pilot scope — our suggested workload: endpoint for 'summary' + a reranking batch job. 100 qps peak, average 18 qps, with typical context length ~800 tokens. does that sound feasible?
[03:10] Devon (Redwood SE): That's very useful — 100 qps peak will need reserved capacity sizing. for the pilot we can size a small Dedicated pool and run the rerank as a batch job during off-peak to validate throughput and cost.
[03:24] Alice (Redwood): timeline suggestion — send security artifacts by Monday (7/28), VPC deep dive and runbook next Wed (7/30), staging window the week of 8/4 and pilot start 8/11 for three weeks. Thoughts?
[03:37] Jenna - Westbridge: Sounds reasonable, we need internal signoff from Legal on the security packet but we'll try to move quickly.
[03:44] Priya - Westbridge: Legal will want to review retention terms and encryption at rest details. can you include sample contract language?
[03:52] Alice (Redwood): Yes i'll include the standard clauses and point to the compliance pack.
[03:56] Marco - Westbridge: A couple of practical Qs: do you require outbound connections to specific IP ranges, and how are failovers handled if a zone goes down?
[04:07] Devon (Redwood SE): We'll provide allowlist IPs for the control plane and show our routing policy — for zone failover we do multi-zone routing and model variant fallback to keep the endpoint up, it's part of the rollout/rollback plan.
[04:22] Samir - Westbridge: Any gotchas around our current stack — we use GKE with Istio and a mix of Python services.
[04:29] Devon (Redwood SE): No big blockers — our SDKs support Python, and we can add a small Istio config snippet for consistent egress. i'll paste that in the runbook.
[04:38] Jenna - Westbridge: For success criteria, we'll validate: P95 < 200ms on summary endpoint, rerank throughput 500 docs/min within cost target, and no PII leakage in logs.
[04:50] Kelsey (Redwood CSM): We'll capture those as pilot KPIs in the shared doc.
[04:54] Priya - Westbridge: Also: can you provide an architecture diagram showing where HSM keys live and where audit logs flow? we need to present that to our auditors.
[05:05] Alice (Redwood): Yes, i'll attach an architecture and sample network diagram with KMS/HSM placement.
[05:12] Jenna - Westbridge: One small transcription note — the doc referenced a "K-V cache" earlier, we think you mean KV cache (keystream) not cash, ha.
[05:19] Devon (Redwood SE): Ha, yeah the transcript sometimes mangles it — K-V cash, KV cache — same thing.
[05:25] Marco - Westbridge: Security aside, would you recommend starting pilot on Hosted API or Dedicated? which gives faster time-to-value?
[05:33] Devon (Redwood SE): Hosted is quickest to stand up; Dedicated gives better predictability for latency and cost. for your P95 needs i recommend Dedicated for pilot staging.
[05:42] Samir - Westbridge: Ok let's plan for a small Dedicated pool for the pilot then.
[05:46] Alice (Redwood): I'll put together an SOW-lite for the pilot and include pricing estimates for Dedicated sizing and retention add-ons and circulate.
[05:55] Jenna - Westbridge: Great. last thing — add our legal contact to the thread so they get the security pack.
[06:00] Alice (Redwood): Will do, please send the contact after the call.
[06:05] Kelsey (Redwood CSM): i'll own the pilot playbook with Devon and keep the weekly check-ins. we'll schedule a 30-minute staging window signoff call week of 8/4.
[06:14] Devon (Redwood SE): ok i'll prepare the runbook and a small benchmark harness for the rerank job. expect a link to a shared sheet.
[06:22] Samir - Westbridge: One more question — are there competitor feature gaps we should know about vs Prodify? we heard they had better observability.
[06:31] Alice (Redwood): we focus on token-level cost/latency analytics and rollout tooling; we'll demo the Console observability next week and show the token breakdown.
[06:41] Jenna - Westbridge: Perfect. thanks everyone.
[06:44] Alice (Redwood): Thanks all, we'll follow up with the security packet and runbook.

Recap / Key decisions: Pilot target start 2025-08-11 for 3 weeks; Dedicated pool recommended; Redwood to provide SOC2, HSM/KMS architecture, VPC checklist, runbook, and pricing estimate.

References: "Pilot runbook (link)" (will be shared), "Security pack (SOC2 + ISO doc)" (to be attached), "Staging runbook spreadsheet (link)".

End of transcript.
file_notes: Customer success kickoff with strong security emphasis; pilot KPIs defined; action items assigned. Transcript intentionally contains real-sounding mis-transcriptions and filler language for authenticity.
